# Variable {#sec-16_variable}

{{< include ../preamble.qmd >}}

## Concepts and intuitions {.unnumbered}

A variable takes different values in different situations

I think the easiest way to understanding a variable is to think of it as a function.
We give an input and we get an output (@sec-08_func).
In the old way f: x -> f(x) = y.
It is important to understand all the values of x and the possible values of y.

This is quite similar as variable in statistics.
x is the object and y is character we measure from that object.

So how about dependent variable, independent variable
Explanatory and response variable
Qualitative, quantitative,
discrete, continuous,
nominal, ordinal

In programming, you will see, integer, numeric (float), and string, boolean, characters, factors (see section programming for others)
